title: Close-out CI verdict names its commit only on green, and a cancelled ancestor run parks it
description:
Two gaps in the close-out's CI read:

1. It names the commit its verdict is about only when CI is GREEN. On red or pending the operator is told a verdict with no subject — the one case where knowing which commit was judged matters most.
2. A cancelled ancestor run parks the close-out rather than being treated as no-verdict-here and walked past.

The ancestor walk was added by 9da precisely so a run-state commit cannot strand the close-out. A cancelled run is the same situation wearing a different label.

From pxc, finding 4e06d8d8.
acceptance_criteria: Every close-out CI verdict names the commit it is about whatever its colour, and a cancelled ancestor is walked past rather than parking the run
